verbs.text: Tossed the vessel like a toy
Dragged him away from the shore

sentences.text: The calm, glassy sea stretched to the horizon like a sheet of hammered silver.
The small, weathered trawler rose and fell on the long, slow swell, as steady as breathing.
Towering, white-capped waves crashed over the deck and swept the barrels overboard.
The raging, relentless tempest tossed the vessel like a toy from one wave to the next.
All night the sea pounded the harbour wall, driven by a fierce, howling gale.
Small, drowsy waves rocked the boat gently, and within minutes he was asleep.
The deep, sapphire sea sparkled like scattered diamonds in the midday sun.
A strong, treacherous undertow dragged him away from the shore, however fiercely he swam.
The water closed over his head, and he sank towards the cold, inky depths.
Wave after wave rolled in from the west and broke into white foam on the reef.
Each wave struck the bow and hurled spray into the air.
A sharp, briny wind filled the taut, white sails.
Sleek, grey dolphins leapt alongside the bow, racing the ship for the sheer joy of it.
Gulls screamed and skimmed the waves in the wake of the fishing boats.
The raft drifted with the tide, a speck on the vast, boundless ocean.
A row of gulls bobbed on the swell like toy ducks in a bath.
The dark, heaving sea churned and seethed beneath a sky the colour of slate.
A shining, silver path of moonlight danced on the water, leading nowhere.
The ship grew smaller until it faded into the distance, leaving only the flat, leaden horizon.
Thick, clammy sea fog crept across the water and put out the lighthouse like a snuffed candle.
The ship slipped out of the harbour on the morning tide.
The water whispered against the hull as the boat slid through the dark.
Thick, white spume boiled around the rocks.
The ferry ploughed through choppy, slate-grey water while the passengers clung to the rail.
Fish flickered through the clear, turquoise shallows like thrown coins.
A wall of water reared above the ship, hung there for a heartbeat, and came thundering down.
For weeks they saw nothing but sea and sky, and the line where the two pretended to meet.
At sunset the sea turned to molten gold, and every wave was tipped with rose.
The harbour was alive with shouting sailors, snapping canvas and the screaming of gulls.
She tasted salt on her lips and felt the deck tilt beneath her feet.
